summary.title: SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for Self-Evolving Agent Skills

details: Agent skills (portable natural-language procedure documents used to adapt a frozen agent) are today hand-written, generated one-shot, or self-revised in loosely controlled loops, and thus not reliably improved over their starting point under feedback.
Goal: train the skill document as the external state of a frozen model with the discipline of a weight-space optimizer, without any weight updates or extra inference-time calls.
SkillOpt: a controllable text-space optimizer over a single skill document, where a separate optimizer LLM turns batches of scored rollouts into structured add/delete/replace edits.

Deep-learning-style controls: rollout batches and reflection minibatches as evidence units, a 'textual learning rate' bounding the number of edits per step (with schedules), a held-out validation gate that accepts a candidate skill only on strict improvement, a rejected-edit buffer as negative feedback, and an epoch-wise slow/meta update writing longitudinal guidance into a protected skill region.
Output is a single compact best_skill.md artifact deployed with a frozen target model and harness.
Six benchmarks: SearchQA, SpreadsheetBench (multi-turn openpyxl/pandas codegen), OfficeQA (tool loops), DocVQA, LiveMathematicianBench, ALFWorld (embodied, up to 50 steps).
Three execution modes: direct chat (skill in system prompt), Codex CLI harness (skill rendered as per-task SKILL.md plus compact execution trace fed to the optimizer), Claude Code CLI harness.
Deterministic train/selection/test splits (split_seed=42); selection split used only for edit acceptance, all reported scores on disjoint test split; ALFWorld omitted under the two CLI harnesses.
Seven target models: GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4-mini, GPT-5.4-nano, GPT-5.2, Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B.
Optimizer model is GPT-5.5 by default; an ablation uses a target-matched optimizer.
4 epochs, rollout batch 40, reflection minibatch 8 (16 parallel analyst workers, merge batch 8), textual learning rate L_t=4 with cosine decay (floor 2), patch edit mode.

Strict validation gate (ties rejected), slow update with 20 sampled tasks per epoch, optimizer-side meta skill (teacher-only), rejected-edit buffer, medium reasoning effort; per-benchmark scaling for small training pools (e.g. LiveMath 35 train items, ALFWorld 39 train tasks).

No skill, expert human-written skill, one-shot LLM skill (GPT-5.5 generated), Trace2Skill (trajectory distillation), TextGrad and GEPA (prompt optimization), EvoSkill (skill-folder evolution, harness settings).
All baselines share target model, test split, and scorer.
Sweeps over training-set size, reflection minibatch size, rollout batch size, learning rate (1-16), schedule (constant/cosine/linear), slow-update sample count.
Component ablations: dynamic vs fixed vs no learning rate; with/without rejected buffer; with/without meta skill and slow update.
Transfer: cross-model (GPT-5.4 skill to mini/nano), cross-harness (Codex <-> Claude Code), cross-benchmark (OlympiadBench skill to Omni-MATH); plus skill length/edit-count/token-cost accounting.

key_findings.finding: SkillOpt is the best or tied-best adaptation method on every evaluated (model, benchmark, harness) cell, with large gains over no skill and over an oracle per-cell baseline.
key_findings.evidence: 52 of 52 cells best or tied. On GPT-5.5 direct chat the six-benchmark average rises 58.8 to 82.3 (+23.5), vs 76.9 for an oracle picking the best of six competing methods per cell (+5.4). Per-benchmark examples: SpreadsheetBench 41.8 to 80.7, OfficeQA 33.1 to 72.1, LiveMath 37.6 to 66.9. Average per-model gain across the seven direct-chat targets is about +17.6 points; in the Codex harness GPT-5.5 gains +24.8 over no skill (+14.0 over EvoSkill) and in Claude Code +19.1 (+3.2 over EvoSkill).

key_findings.finding: The controls that make skill editing behave like a training loop (bounded edit budget, validation gate, rejected-edit buffer, slow/meta update) matter far more than the exact batch or schedule settings.
key_findings.evidence: Removing the learning rate drops scores to 84.6/75.7/57.3 vs 87.1/77.5/61.3 default on SearchQA/SpreadsheetBench/LiveMath; removing the rejected buffer costs 1.6/4.6/2.4 points; removing both meta skill and slow update drops SpreadsheetBench from 77.5 to 55.0. In contrast, sweeping reflection minibatch 1-32, rollout batch 8-full-epoch, lr 1-16, and constant/cosine/linear schedules keeps SearchQA within about 85-87 and SpreadsheetBench within about 73-81.

key_findings.finding: Optimized skill artifacts are reusable: they transfer positively across model scales, across execution harnesses, and to a nearby math benchmark without further optimization.
key_findings.evidence: All transfer rows are above the target's no-skill baseline: GPT-5.4-trained SpreadsheetBench skill gives +9.4 on GPT-5.4-mini (82% of the in-domain gain) and +3.0 on nano; a Codex-trained spreadsheet skill gives +59.7 on Claude Code (22.1 to 81.8, exceeding the 80.4 in-domain reference) and the reverse direction +43.6; an OlympiadBench skill gives +3.7/+1.8/+1.3 on Omni-MATH across three GPT scales; on LiveMath GPT-5.4-nano the transferred skill (28.8) beats in-domain (27.2).

key_findings.finding: Large gains come from very few accepted edits producing compact, procedural, auditable skill documents.
key_findings.evidence: Final best_skill.md files are 379 to 1,995 tokens (median about 920) after only 1-4 accepted edits; LiveMath's +29.3 and OfficeQA's +39.0 point gains each come from a single accepted edit. Training cost per absolute test point ranges from 0.6M tokens (SpreadsheetBench) to 46.4M (DocVQA), paid once offline. Extracted rules are procedural (e.g. write evaluated static values across the full target range; keep a horizon-aware visited/frontier ledger) rather than instance-specific.

key_findings.finding: A stronger optimizer model improves the trained skill monotonically, but the loop itself, not teacher-to-student distillation, supplies most of the value.
key_findings.evidence: With everything else fixed, GPT-5.5 as optimizer beats a target-matched optimizer on all four tested cells (e.g. SpreadsheetBench GPT-5.4-nano +19.0 vs +11.9; SearchQA nano +19.0 vs +14.1), yet the target-matched optimizer still recovers 56-74% of the strong-optimizer gain; the optimizer is used only offline, adding no deployment cost.
